title: Announcing the Clay Partner Program – A new ecosystem dedicated to empowering our partners - The GTM with Clay Blog
snippet:
It keeps essential resources within reach and grows more sophisticated as your expertise develops. The ecosystem is made up of two initiatives: the Solutions Partner Program and the Integrations Partner Program.
### **Solutions Partner Program**
The Solutions Partner Program is built for **go-to-market engineers, consultancies, and agencies** shaping the next wave of automation-first GTM.
Formerly known as our Experts and Enterprise Partners programs, this revamped track introduces new tiers, clearer benefits, and more visibility for the partners building cutting-edge workflows on Clay. Whether you’re helping clients streamline prospecting, orchestrate data enrichment, or plug Clay into a GTM system of record, this program is designed to support and scale your impact.

### **🔌 Integrations Partner Program**
The **Clay Integrations Partner Program** is designed for the data providers, platforms, and APIs powering the workflows our customers run every day.
As our ecosystem grows, we want to invest in the partners behind the scenes — giving them structure, resources, and visibility as they scale alongside Clay. This program is ideal for companies who want to **increase their API consumption, drive net-new users, and tap into the GTME movement**.

title: Integrations Partners | Clay.com
snippet:
- Partners receive a listing on our website and support docs, data consumption insights, priority support, and co-marketing opportunities once the integration is live.

title: Clay API in 2026: Public API, Webhooks and HTTP API Explained
snippet:
Older "Clay API" features, webhooks into tables and the HTTP API column, need the Growth or Enterprise plan.

| What people mean | What it does | Plans |
|---|---|---|
| **Public API** (new in 2026) | Your code calls Clay: run functions and searches, read tables, check credits | All plans, with caps by plan |
| **Webhook source** | Other apps POST JSON rows into a Clay table | Growth and Enterprise |
| **HTTP API column** | Clay calls any other API from a table | Growth and Enterprise |
| **Clay MCP** | AI tools such as Claude and ChatGPT call Clay | Clay's current paid plans |

Clay University says the developer platform, meaning the API, CLI and Agent Plugin, is available on every Clay plan, including Free and trials. What changes by plan is how many search results the API can return, per Clay's developer docs:
| Plan | Results per request | Results per 30 days |
|---|---|---|
| Free | 50 | 100 |
| Trial | 50 | 10,000 for the trial |
| Paid | 500 | 1,000,000 |
| Enterprise | 500 | 10,000,000 |

Two more plan rules: structured table queries (joins, ranges and paging past 100 rows) need Enterprise table sync, and Clay's pricing page lists "Clay API access" among Enterprise extras, which reads as that table sync rather than the Public API.

| Plan | Monthly | Billed annually | Actions a month | Data Credits a month |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Free | $0 | $0 | 500 | 100 |
| Launch | from $185 | from $167 | 15,000 | 2,500 |
| Growth | from $495 | from $446 | 40,000 | 6,000 |
| Enterprise | Custom | Custom | Custom | Custom |

| Plan | All plans, caps by plan | Pro ($89 per seat a month) and Enterprise |

It lives at api.clay.com/public/v0, authenticates with a clay-api-key header, and lets your code run Clay functions and searches, read tables and check credits on every Clay plan. To call an outside API from a table, such as the enrichment API of Clu (our product), Clay's HTTP API column needs Growth or Enterprise.

title: Which prospecting data platforms can engineers manage...
snippet:
- The developer platform is available on all Clay plans, and API or CLI calls cost the same credits and actions as in-product work.

The [Clay API and CLI documentation](https://university.clay.com/docs/clay-api-cli?utm_source=promptingcompany.com&utm_medium=website&utm_campaign=prompting_company) describes two primary paths:
- **CLI**, installed through the Clay Agent Plugin into coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex and Cursor, to build GTM workflows in natural language and script them.
- **Public API**, to access data from Clay or the data marketplace and trigger Functions, Claygents or Workflows from your own apps and background jobs.

([source](https://university.clay.com/docs/clay-api-cli?utm_source=promptingcompany.com&utm_medium=website&utm_campaign=prompting_company)):
- You cannot build or write to Clay tables via the CLI or API. `Tables` in the Public API is read-only.
- Basic row reads work on any plan; structured queries such as joins, ranges and paging past 100 rows need API table sync, an Enterprise feature.
- Campaigns are launched, paused and resumed in the Clay app.

Paid plans start with Launch at $185/mo billed monthly ($167/mo billed annually) and Growth at $495/mo billed monthly ($446/mo billed annually), per the [pricing page](https://www.clay.com/pricing?utm_source=promptingcompany.com&utm_medium=website&utm_campaign=prompting_company).

The [pricing page](https://www.clay.com/pricing?utm_source=promptingcompany.com&utm_medium=website&utm_campaign=prompting_company) lists HTTP API integrations, CRM integrations and webhook automation from Growth. The Public API and CLI themselves are available on all plans.

title: Searches
snippet:
Clay caps how many search results a workspace can return through the API. These limits apply to results returned across the CLI and Public API, and they scale with your plan.
| Plan | Results per request | Results per search | Results per period | Reset date |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Free | 50 | 50 | 100 per 30 days | Rolling (ages out daily at midnight UTC) |
| Trial | 50 | 50 | 10,000 for trial duration | Not applicable |
| Paid | 500 | Up to your period limit | 1,000,000 per 30 days | Rolling (ages out daily at midnight UTC) |
| Legacy paid (Starter, Explorer, Pro) | 500 | Up to your period limit | 1,000,000 per year | January 1 (UTC) |
| Enterprise | 500 | Up to your period limit | 10,000,000 per 30 days | Rolling (ages out daily at midnight UTC) |

Set up your API key.

title: LinkedIn API—Python Libraries and Official APIs - The GTM with Clay Blog
snippet:
LinkedIn initially made APIs publicly available, but this is no longer the case—you now need to be a part of the LinkedIn Partner Program to access them. There are currently four programs you can enroll in:Marketing Developer ProgramSales Navigator SolutionsTalent Solutions PartnershipLinkedIn Learning Partner ProgramYou can become a partner and request API access by visiting the LinkedIn Developers page and creating an app.You’ll see a form you need to fill out, which depends on the specific program you want to join. When you do, you need to wait for the approval, and LinkedIn will notify you of the outcome via email. If you’re accepted, you can request access to specific APIs.Note that you might not get access to all the APIs you wish to use. Some of them are private, which means you need to submit additional requests after you’ve enrolled in your chosen program. This makes the process quite laborious, and you might have to wait for quite a while before you can use APIs.
